News.title: Russian soldier threatens to turn weapons on Putin as Vlad may face another rebellion with troops fuming over war
News.content:
A RUSSIAN soldier has threatened to turn weapons on Vladimir Putin as the Kremlin tyrant stares down the barrel of another rebellion.

One veteran who vented his outrage at the bloody invasion of Ukraine in a viral social media post has vowed to spark an uprising if Putin doesn’t “tell the truth”.





The ex-soldier, called Alexander Lunin, declared he would launch a rebellion on Putin’s regime if the president didn’t meet with him to discuss the abuse of soldiers.

In the video which has been viewed over 11 million times, the veteran said thousands of soldiers were being held in pits and tortured “for refusing to carry out stupid, suicidal orders”.

He also said service members were being abused for refusing to hand over money to their commanders.

Lunin warned “the consequences will be very serious” if he wasn’t set up for meeting with Putin on live TV.

Lunin said: “If I don’t arrive at the Kremlin in the near future and speak live on the air right next to you, the army will turn its weapons against the Kremlin.

“I’m merely passing along the message.”



He claimed that high ranking army and security officials had asked him to film the statement clip.

Kremlin mouthpiece Dmitry Peskov said he had heard about the viral video but claimed neither he nor Putin had watched it yet.

“The phrasing sounds rather bizarre. We need to see it first,” Peskov said.



Lunin is a 39-year-old Ukraine war veteran from the Voronezh region in southern Russia, according to local media.

It comes after a failed uprising by the Wagner Group three years ago.

The group’s boss Yevgeny Prigozhin had vowed to “punish” Russia after he blamed the Kremlin for a deadly missile attack on one of his training camps in the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut.

The mercenary head then left Russia as part of a deal to end his uprising with charges against him being dropped.

But he was then killed when his private jet was blown out of the sky.



It also comes amid a string of setbacks for Putin’s war.

Ukraine launched devastating strikes on a key Russian oil depot earlier this month.

And on Thursday, Kyiv turned up the heat on Russia and unleashed a 40-day blitz “aimed at securing an end to the war”.

Russia suffered one of the biggest nighttime attacks – with air defences in a dozen regions, as well as Russian-occupied Crimea, the Black Sea and the Azov Sea, intercepting 660 Ukrainian drones.

The barrage came hours after Volodymyr Zelensky said ⁠he had approved a massive ⁠campaign in an effort to turn the tables on Russia‘s grinding war of aggression.



“I approved a 40-day operation ‌by the Service ‌to influence the aggressor state in order ⁠to press for an end to the war,” the Ukrainian President said on Telegram.

His announcement followed his meeting with SBU chief Yevhenii Khmara, who reported on Ukraine’s “plan for long-range sanctions, medium-range sanctions” – a term used by Kyiv to describe its drone strikes.

For months, Ukraine has ‌carried out devastating attacks on targets in ⁠Russia or Russian-held ‌areas, with a heavy focus on ‌the oil ​industry.

The Security Service said it deployed drones to strike Russian navy ships and air defence radars in Kerch, an important port city in Crimea.

Two reconnaissance and mine-laying ships, the Volga and the Vyatka, and the cargo-passenger ferry Petropavlovsk, were the targets, the agency said.



Fires were reported at a chemical plant in Novomoskovsk, which supplies the war machine with materials for explosives and artillery ammunition.

Meanwhile, the power station supplying it with electricity was also blown up.

And a shipbuilding plant in Kerch was also blown up.

This is close to Putin’s £3billion Crimean Bridge which was closed again today amid fears the giant crossing is to be targeted by Ukraine.

Early this week, Zelensky said that S-400 and S-500 anti-ballistic systems, backed by Pantsir air defence systems, have been deployed in “hundreds of launchers” around the region to protect it.



“Right now, the Russian leadership is pulling more air defence systems toward Moscow, toward Valdai, and toward Putin’s bridge across the Kerch Strait – at the expense of air defences in other directions,” he added.

He described this redistribution as a sign that Russia is willing to thin out defences across much of its territory in order to reinforce the capital and a small number of priority locations.

News.title: Man, 31, arrested for ‘murder’ of girl, 3, had ‘bandages on chest’ as horrified neighbours left in ‘complete disbelief’
News.content:
TRAGIC TOT Man, 31, arrested for ‘murder’ of girl, 3, had ‘bandages on chest’ as horrified neighbours left in ‘complete disbelief’

NEIGHBOURS have been left in “total disbelief” at the death of a toddler at a block of flats in leafy Surrey.

Flowers have been left at the entrance to Syward Place, Chertsey, where a three-year-old girl was found dead.





A 31-year-old man was taken to hospital with serious injuries before being arrested on suspicion of murder.

Police have confirmed they’re not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident.

An investigation has been launched, with the Major Crime Team leading the probe.

A resident of the block said: “It happened on the ground floor. I saw them take him away. He was wearing an oxygen mask and had bandages on his abdomen.





“He seemed calm as they were putting him into the back of a police car.

“This place is full of young professionals. The flats are very plush. Some studios but mostly one or two bedroom. There are lots of families here too.”

Another resident of the block of flats said: “Everyone is in shock. When it happens on your doorstep, you don’t know how to react. I feel so sorry for the little girl.

“I don’t know the family or what happened, but I did see and hear lots of police last night when I came back from work.”

Local mum Susan Williamson, 31, left flowers at the scene and said: “It’s just so horribly sad.



“I’m a mum and I just wanted to come down here to pay my respects.

“Everyone is in a state of shock about what has happened. This is a nice area with good people. Things like this don’t usually happen in Chertsey.”

In 2023, it was reported there were plans to house asylum seeker families in the block.

However, the plans were scrapped a year later following a petition from local residents.

The steward of Chertsey Social Club, which is on the opposite side of the road from the flats, Kevin Quirk, said: “I came outside at around 6pm and there were police cars and ambulances everywhere. They had taped off the area.



“It was very unusual to see so many police in one place. They even had an air ambulance land nearby, but I don’t think it was used.

“It’s very unusual to see police cars in this area. It’s so quiet. It’s a really safe community, so when you see that many police cars it does shock you.

“There are lots of families in that block. It used to be offices but was converted a few years back.

“At one time they were going to house people from overseas, immigrants, in these flats, but the residents kicked off so much they abandoned that idea.”

The man was found at the address suffering from serious injuries and was arrested on suspicion of murder.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

There is no longer a police presence outside the building.

A message left at the scene read: “RIP beautiful girl. Too good for this earth. May you rest in paradise.”

News.title: King Charles ‘deeply saddened’ by Venezuela earthquakes as death toll climbs to 920 with thousands still missing
News.content:
QUAKE TRAGEDY King Charles ‘deeply saddened’ by Venezuela earthquakes as death toll climbs to 920 with thousands still missing

THE King and Queen have said they are “deeply saddened” by the devastating earthquakes that have struck Venezuela, killing nearly 1,000 people.

In a personal message to the Venezuelan people, King Charles expressed the royal couple’s “profound sympathy” to those who have lost loved ones, homes and livelihoods in the disaster.





He wrote: “To the people of Venezuela,

“My wife and I were deeply saddened to learn of the devastating earthquakes that have struck your country, and of the tragic loss of life and suffering they have caused.

“At this most difficult of times, we send our profound sympathy to all those who have lost loved ones, homes and livelihoods.

“Our special thoughts are with the injured, those awaiting news of family and friends, and the emergency responders working tirelessly to support those in desperate need.

“We greatly admire the resilience and strength of the Venezuelan people and send our most heartfelt condolences to all those affected by this terrible tragedy.”

A rare double earthquake ravaged Venezuela on Wednesday.



Rescue teams are racing against time to find tens of thousands of people feared trapped beneath the rubble after the two devastating earthquakes tore through the country.

The death toll has climbed to at least 920, while more than 4,300 people have been injured following the back-to-back quakes that struck on Wednesday night.

Officials fear the number of victims will continue to rise, with at least 58,000 people reported missing.

The worst-hit areas include La Guaira, a coastal region north of the capital, Caracas, where entire neighbourhoods have been reduced to rubble.

The US military has deployed elite search and rescue teams to help locate survivors buried beneath collapsed buildings.



Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US had prepared a “whole government response”.

“It’ll be big, it’ll be fast and it’ll be effective”, he said.

The disaster began when a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck, followed just minutes later by a magnitude 7.5 tremor – the most powerful to hit Venezuela in more than a century.



Satellite images reveal the scale of the destruction, showing entire districts obliterated with buildings flattened to the ground.

Residents woke on Thursday to scenes of devastation, with roads split apart, homes destroyed and helicopters circling overhead as emergency crews searched for survivors.

The US Geological Survey estimates the final death toll could reach anywhere between 10,000 and 100,000 people.

The United Nations warned that a “massive collective effort” will be needed to respond to the catastrophe, as leaders from Mexico, Qatar, Brazil, Spain, Portugal and Canada pledged to send emergency aid.

US Marine Corps Major General Kevin J. Jarrad arrived in Caracas on Friday to oversee the American military’s disaster relief operation.



Meanwhile, elite search-and-rescue squad USA-01 is preparing to deploy 79 personnel, 70,000 pounds of specialist equipment and six sniffer dogs to the quake-hit region.

What is a doublet-earthquake? A DOUBLET-earthquake is a single earthquake event that features two or more major shocks instead of just one.

The twin shocks have nearly identical magnitudes, usually within 0.4 of each other.

Wednesday’s initial rocking was the first event in a doublet, with the magnitude 7.2 foreshock followed just 39 seconds later by a larger 7.5 magnitude main shock.

Both shocks originate from the exact same fault line and rupture zone.

Because they come from the same spot, they leave almost identical “fingerprints” on seismometers.

Traditional aftershocks are much weaker, but doublets maintain full, devastating strength.

They happen when a tearing fault line hits a massive, rigid chunk of crust called an asperity.

The first quake fails to release all the tectonic stress, jamming all that leftover pressure onto the stuck blockage.

Unable to hold the sudden pressure, the blockage violently snaps to trigger the second big quake.

They double the duration of violent shaking, often collapsing buildings already weakened by the first strike

The team, made up of firefighters, paramedics, engineers and canine handlers, has previously responded to major natural disasters, including the 2010 Haiti earthquake.

The twin earthquakes struck around 100 miles west of Caracas, triggering scenes of panic as terrified residents fled swaying buildings.

Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez declared a nationwide state of emergency within hours of the disaster.

But desperate mother-of-three Dayana Delgado questioned where the heavy machinery promised by officials had gone.



“I want to know where my child is, if he’s trapped or in a shelter”, she said of her missing eight-year-old son.

Another distraught woman said her daughter remained trapped inside a 12-storey building.

“There are people alive in there and no one is coming to save them,” she said.

Across the country, families have put up missing-person posters and circulated handwritten lists of names in a frantic search for loved ones.

Venezuelan state television broadcast dramatic rescue footage, including the moment emergency crews pulled a woman alive from beneath a concrete slab after only one of her feet could be seen sticking out.



The coastal town of La Guaira has suffered some of the worst destruction, with several apartment blocks left as hollow shells.

Interim leader Rodríguez said the official death toll does not yet include victims in La Guaira because rescue crews are still struggling to clear the wreckage and recover bodies.

She also announced the creation of a $200million fund, financed through the International Monetary Fund, to help rebuild homes, hospitals and infrastructure over the coming weeks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tom Fletcher, under-secretary-general for UN Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief, said: “Even before these earthquakes, nearly eight million people in Venezuela were in need of humanitarian support.

“This disaster risks deepening existing vulnerabilities. Sustained international support for humanitarian organisations responding on the ground is essential and urgent.”

News.title: Who can blame Trump for being in the dark about what Burnham REALLY thinks when us Brits don’t know either
News.content:
“I GUESS he was the mayor of a town” was not exactly the introduction to the world stage Andy Burnham might have hoped for from the most famous room in the world.

“I hear he’s extremely liberal, extremely,” mused Donald Trump in the Oval Office this week, before admitting he barely knew a thing about the man seizing control of one of the United States’ most important allies.





Yet given our Prime Minister Un-Elect is a relative unknown to the voters of Britain — they don’t really know what he really wants, thinks or believes either — who can blame the leader of the free world for being in the dark?

After months of bitter wrangling between the White House and No10 as Sir Keir Starmer’s grip on the Special Relationship was slowly fed into a diplomatic blender, things need sorting quickly.

But this new pair are already on a fresh collision course.

In his cagey campaign in Makerfield, one glint of Burnham’s policy was tax relief for struggling British industries by increasing taxes on online tech giants.

Well, the verdict on that is already in, with President Trump warning last night: “Any country that imposes such a Tax will immediately be met with a 100% TARIFF on any and all Goods sent to the United States of America.

“This TARIFF will supersede Trade Deals made with the Country, whether implemented, signed, or not.”

Well, back to the drawing board there . . .

And where does Burnham stand on Keir Starmer’s horrific Chagos surrender deal?



Begging National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell — the architect of the shameful giveaway of territory — to stay in post doesn’t bode well.

On Iran, Israel, Ukraine or defence spending, you name it, the world is in the dark at what Burnham — and by default soon enough Britain — now thinks.

More of the same clearly won’t cut it, but where I fear things may shift risks an even worse rupture in our vital transatlantic alliance. And that’s before we even look into Burnham’s past.



If not before, Britain’s next PM will meet Donald Trump in Miami at the G20 in mid-December and by then I suspect the President might well have found out a little more about his new colleague.

Sadly it only took a week from Trump taking office for Burnham to call for him to be impeached for “gross incompetence”.

“Hope so,” Britain’s next PM chirped just seven days after the US President was first sworn in.

A few months later in 2017, Burnham was off on one again, demanding the “deeply troubling” leader of the free world be BANNED from ever visiting Manchester because of “extreme views emanating from the Oval Office”.

“I call on the Prime Minister to withdraw the invitation of a state visit,” he added.



“It is a matter of principle that I don’t meet people who distribute hateful, extremist material.

“There are communities in the UK, many different communities, who will feel deeply unsettled about this president’s visit to the UK because of things he has said and the way he has treated people at his own borders . . . and if it looks to them like all politicians are rushing to a state banquet to lavish praise and fall at his knee, that sends another message that politicians don’t represent them.”

For what it’s worth, Trump’s border policies remain spectacularly popular with voters, but when did that ever stop some lefty virtue-signalling?

The diatribes “emanating” from Manchester towards Washington did not stop there, in fact they continued through Trump’s first term.



As that ended, Burnham was unrelenting: “Any UK politician who gave Trump the time of day should be ashamed,” he tweeted in 2021.

Just this month Burnham was attacking America’s “polarised, poisonous politics”, despite admitting in his 2024 book: “Whether we like it or not, Donald Trump and Nigel Farage have been effective in connecting with people who feel politicians have neglected the place where they live.”

The White House has been quick out of the traps already, with some withering barbs about Burnham’s comments.

No-nonsense Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly hit back: “Left-wing policies of unfettered migration and destructive globalism have made once-great European cities unrecognisable allowing criminals to run wild and antisemitism to thrive.



“President Trump saved the United States from such destruction when he was elected, and he has rightfully warned other world leaders that western civilisation will continue to erode if they don’t quickly reverse course.”

Not a great start there.

But is there hope that things can be patched up?

It’s worth noting that some of the most unlikely bromances the President has struck up are with handsome left-wingers, whose good looks he often awkwardly lavishes.

Hardcore socialist New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani openly called Trump a fascist and still got the red carpet treatment.



The President likes winners too, but Burnham would actually have to put himself forward to democratic scrutiny to tick that box.

While I suspect past barbs can be brushed under the carpet, I fear the policy battles will be a much tougher fix.

SCENES of joy are playing out across America as European fans drink cities dry and discover air-conditioning.

Scotland fans did us proud by downing all the Sam Adams beer that Boston could offer, while hard-partying Texan pals have texted their grudging support for how hard England fans hit it in Dallas.

But spare a thought for the deranged leftists who can’t even take an evening off to watch the football because of their politics.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Democrats grapple uncomfortably with World Cup success,” read one dreary headline in the US press this week.

Because the Trump administration has put on a good show, they have to go and cry in the dark. Take 90 minutes off, guys, for your own sanity . . .

News.title: Government farce as Home Secretary bans her own immigration minister from official papers rather than sacking him
News.content:
SIR Keir Starmer’s lame-duck Government descended into farce yesterday after the Home Secretary failed to sack her own immigration minister — and instead banned him from seeing official documents.

Shabana Mahmood imposed the extraordinary restriction on Mike Tapp as the PM refused to remove him for a newspaper article on migration.





He will stay in post but cannot view Home Office papers or hold official meetings without approval.

Mr Tapp had called for foreign care workers to be exempt from Labour’s hardline settlement reforms.

Ms Mahmood was unaware of the article before it was published and asked Sir Keir to sack him for a Ministerial Code breach.

But No 10 made it clear that the final decision rested with the PM.

A spokesman said: “It is not for any individual Secretary of State to determine whether the Ministerial Code has been followed, it is a matter for the PM alone.”

Earlier, Mr Tapp insisted on social media: “I won’t be intimidated to drop my views. Stay classy!”

He also compared the row to fighting the Taliban in a post which he later deleted.

Ms Mahmood’s failed bid to force out Mr Tapp triggered a backlash inside Labour, with one Government aide branding her “completely shameless and dishonourable” after she spent months publicly piling pressure on Sir Keir Starmer.



The Home Secretary was among the first Cabinet ministers to tell Sir Keir his time was up after Labour’s local election drubbing.

The row has also reignited Labour’s bitter argument over plans to make many migrants wait ten years instead of five before qualifying for permanent settlement.

News.title: Kemi’s eye-catching defence policy shows strong leadership – she must keep banging the drum for strivers over skivers
News.content:
Kemi have a go

BRITAIN is crying out for strong leadership.

After a week in which she dished out another brutal bashing to Labour’s floundering leadership, Kemi Badenoch’s latest eye-catching policy shows she understands the challenge.





For years, military reservists have been penalised by the Treasury for doing the right thing.

The Tory leader says she will attract more part-time soldiers by instead making the first 30 days of service per financial year completely tax free.

Crucially, Kemi recognises that this spending commitment should be funded by bringing back the two-child benefits cap.

Who could argue against a nurse serving part-time as an Army reservist having more money in her pocket, instead of the cash going to workless large families?



Just as she faced down wailing Labour ministers furious at her portrayal of them as class-war zealots, so Kemi must keep banging the drum for the strivers over the skivers.

There are no easy answers to Britain’s deep-rooted problems — none of which are likely to be fixed by Andy Burnham.

The more honest Kemi is about making tough choices, the greater her chances of persuading people to vote Tory again.

Spinless Tapp

THE dysfunction at the top of Labour would be laughable were it not so serious.



Treacherous ministers who queued up to knife Sir Keir Starmer are now fighting like rats in a sack for a job from PM-in-waiting Andy Burnham.

While their ludicrous squabbles play out, voters’ concerns are forgotten.

People want the boats stopped and illegal migration tackled.

Yet the Home Office is in a bizarre standoff between Shabana Mahmood and her immigration minister Mike Tapp.

The Home Secretary wants Tapp fired for making public the secret asylum plan in a bid to suck up to Burnham.



Starmer won’t act because Tapp has been loyal, while Mahmood told the PM to quit. Who, actually, is in charge?

Labour pledged to end the chaos.

If anything, Burnham’s bid for power has made it even worse.

Red Ed alert

THE mayhem is unlikely to end if Ed Miliband becomes Chancellor.

It’s rare that businesses and the unions sing from the same hymn sheet.



But heavy industry union chiefs at the GMB and the likes of Iceland supermarket boss Richard Walker are united against Miliband taking charge of the Treasury.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Miliband has already sacrificed thousands of jobs on the altar of Net Zero.

Burnham must know that handing his chum the keys to Number 11 would inflict similar damage on the nation’s finances.

News.title: Brit Tiktoker facing death penalty in Dubai left without lawyer or translator five days after arrest, sparking concern
News.content:
A BRIT accused of killing her boyfriend in Dubai has still not been allowed to see a lawyer five days after her arrest.

Brooke George, 23, faces the death penalty if convicted of the murder of William Treeby, 26.





The influencer, from Gravesend, Kent, was arrested on Monday and has had no legal representation or translator.

Brooke, who had more than 100,000 followers on TikTok, claims she acted in self-defence.

Radha Stirling, of campaign group Detained in Dubai, said: This case is deeply personal to me.

“Years ago, I was the last person to speak to a man in Dubai before he was executed by firing squad.

“We spoke just thirty minutes before his death, and I have never forgotten that conversation.

“Knowing Brooke is facing a charge that carries the death penalty, I cannot overstate how concerned I am for her.

“Brooke is just 23 years old. Only days ago she experienced what she describes as a terrifying and traumatic ordeal.

“Instead of receiving the legal and psychological support that would ordinarily be available to a young woman claiming she acted in self defence after alleged abuse, she remains without proper access to legal representation.



“Every day that passes places her at an even greater disadvantage.”

She said the UAE criminal justice system “often fails to recognise the realities of coercion and domestic violence”.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said: “We are supporting a British national detained in the UAE.”

News.title: Hundreds of unemployed youngsters set for theme park jobs in new employment push
News.content:
HUNDREDS of jobless youngsters will get the chance to start their careers at Britain’s biggest theme parks under a new jobs drive.

Merlin Entertainments will create 300 opportunities over the next three years for young people claiming Universal Credit.





The jobs will be based at attractions including Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, Chessington World of Adventures and Legoland Windsor.

Young recruits could find themselves working on everything from rollercoaster engineering and ride maintenance to retail, hospitality and guest services.

The move is part of the Government’s Youth Guarantee, aimed at helping more young people into work or training.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said: “Every young person deserves the chance to earn or learn, and we’re supporting great British employers to back our young people, and put them on track for success.



“Merlin Entertainment are doing just that, with hundreds of opportunities at their attractions across the country – providing the launchpad for young people to get their careers off to a flying start.”

Merlin boss Fiona Eastwood said: “This is a practical, positive step that helps businesses like Merlin invest in young people with confidence while giving them the skills, experience and support to grow and progress.”

A million young people in Britain are now classed as NEET — not in education, employment or training.

Damning figures reveal the youth jobs crisis is deepening, with warnings that a “lost generation” could reach 1.25million within five years unless urgent action is taken.



The latest data from the Office for National Statistics shows 1,012,000 people aged 16 to 24 were NEET in the first three months of 2026.

That is up 89,000 on the same period last year and up 55,000 on the previous quarter.

It means 13.5% of all young people in the UK — roughly one in eight — are currently locked out of work, education and training.

Young men are bearing the brunt of the crisis.

News.title: UK weather live: June heat record broken for third day in a row as temperatures hit 37.3C
News.content:
Heatwave conditions continue with a red warning for extreme heat again in place by the Met Office, with temperatures reaching record-breaking highs of 37.3C

Temperature records for June have been broken for the third day in a row as the UK swelters in a heatwave.

A provisional temperature of 37.3C has been recorded in Santon Downham, Suffolk, the Met Office said. A red warning for extreme heat has been in place for the third consecutive day.

Friday afternoon saw the country split by extreme weather conditions, with ferocious thunderstorms and lightning storms wreaking havoc in parts of the north, while the south-east remained in the grip of a scorching heatwave.

More than 63,000 lightning strikes have been recorded over the past 24 hours, the Met Office said, one of which caused a fire after striking a nursing home in Glastonbury. Passengers in Edinburgh were forced to flee an early-morning train after a terrifying lightning strike, while a tram in Sheffield was also taken out of service after being hit.

News.title: Zia Yusuf 'blocked by his OWN party from standing as an MP' as BBC Question Time audience laugh
News.content:
Zia Yusuf 'blocked by his OWN party from standing as an MP' as BBC Question Time audience laugh

During this week's episode of BBC Question Time, filmed in Kettering, Reform UK Home Affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf seemed to suggest he was 'blocked by his own party from standing as an MP'

View 2 Images Zia Yusuf says Reform UK blocked him running as MP in BBC Question Time bombshell (Image: BBC)

The BBC Question Time crowd erupted into laughter and applause when Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf failed to answer if he was "rejected" by Reform UK to run as MP - but his silence spoke volumes.

‌



On the panel, Labour chair of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee Emily Thornberry; Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake; Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf and economist and journalist Stephanie Flanders.

‌



The debate heated up when Conservative Party Chairman Kevin Hollinrake accused Zia of hypocrisy for never standing for public office whilst simultaneously criticising those who have. Hollinrake asked: “Why have you not stood in some of the by-elections, the opportunities you’ve had round the country to get elected?”

‌



View 2 Images Conservative Party Chairman Kevin Hollinrake (Image: BBC)

Yusuf shot back cryptically: “It is interesting that you think all of the country’s problems seem to be down to whether I have stood in a by-election or not. What makes you think I never put myself above the parapet?”

When presented with the fact that he had not been named as a candidate in any by-election in recent years, Yusuf responded: “So anybody that wishes to stand in a by-election automatically gets the chance to do so. Maybe that is what happens in the Conservative Party where it is just cronyism and nothing else matters, mate, but I think you have made a lot of big assumptions.”

He added: “We have a process for standing in parliamentary by-elections and all I would say is that coming after me for not standing in a parliamentary by-election is incorrect and hugely presumptuous.”

Bruce concluded: “I am taking from what you have said that you have put your name forward to stand in a by-election but you have not been selected. If I am wrong tell me now.”
